findings.message: normalize_path strips the surrounding quotes but never decodes the C-style octal escapes inside git's quoted path, so a tracked src/café.py is reported as src/caf/303/251.py. The mangled path no longer matches the work tree, so complexity_map silently assigns complexity 0 and the report names a file that does not exist. Git quotes every non-ASCII path by default (core.quotePath=true), so any repos

--min-score accepts nan and inf because the validator only rejects values below zero. nan makes every item.score >= args.min_score comparison false, so the command silently prints an empty report; inf hides every row. The README promises invalid numeric flags exit 2, so reject non-finite input here.
findings.patch_old:
if value < 0:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError("must be non-negative")
findings.patch_new:
if not 0 <= value < float("inf"):
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError("must be a finite non-negative number")

findings.message: Extend the numeric-flag regression test with the non-finite inputs; otherwise the new nan/inf rejection has no test and can silently regress.

Only --exclude is exercised; the documented --include branch in _matches has no test, so an inverted include filter would still pass the suite. Add a case that asks for --include src/* and expects only src/app.py.

findings.message: A malformed --since value (for example 'not a date') is forwarded to git verbatim; git accepts it and returns an empty log, so the user sees 'No hotspots found' with guidance to widen --since instead of a signal that the date itself is unparseable. Warning when --since is set and churn comes back empty, or pre-validating the date, would separate a syntax error from a genuinely quiet range.
